title: Quota Safeguard & Namespace Keying Walkthrough - Celestia Ventures
next_steps: Share SOC 2 and network architecture diagram
Schedule PoC benchmark run (100k tokens/day footprint)
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Celestia through console demos for org/project keying, quota safeguards and namespace-based routing. Customer is evaluating dedicated vs hosted, cares about burst protection and data residency. Next: pricing and security pack; PoC benchmark to follow.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-30 15:00 PDT — Duration 48m. Attendees listed above.

[00:00] Lena: hi everyone, thanks for taking the time today, this is lena from Redwood, i'll let marco kick off the product side and then we'll walk through the console and some recommended policies.

[00:18] Marco: hey team, marco here, senior solutions eng. quick agenda, 1) high-level keying patterns — org keys vs project keys, 2) quota safeguard and burst lanes, 3) namespace routing demo in the console, 4) quick walkthrough of Optimize suggestions for quantization/batching. and Q&A.

[00:35] Priya: sounds good. we invited ethan and samira cause they'll own infra and security questions. our main pain: unpredictable third‑party bots causing spikes, cost spikes, and we need per-team isolation + some regional routing for EU data.

[00:52] Lena: great, that maps to a couple of patterns we see a lot. quick q — are you leaning toward hosted or dedicated for the PoC?

[01:02] Priya: leaning hosted to start but if latency and compliance are okay, we may move to dedicated. timeline Q: 6–8 weeks to evaluate.

[01:12] Marco: perfect. i'll show both hosted controls and how the same model of keys/policies apply to Dedicated or Private deploy.

[01:30] Marco: first, org key = top-level billing/owner, project keys = teams or applications. you can attach different quota policies to each, e.g., projectA has 20 rps steady, burst lane of 80 rps for 30s. the console shows that as a policy row.

[01:52] Ethan: can burst lanes be throttled by token volume or request concurrency?

[02:00] Marco: yes — you can set both token-based quotas and concurrency thresholds. a common pattern is tokens/day + concurrency cap + short burst allowance. the burst is enforced by a leaky-bucket at the API gateway level so it degrades gracefully.

[02:18] Samira: how do you prevent noisy tenants from exhausting capacity? isolation through projects + priority lanes?

[02:26] Marco: exactly. we recommend project-level quotas for tenant isolation, plus an org-wide guardrail that will auto-failover to a cheaper model variant if capacity is exceeded. think of it as graceful degradation: route to quantized model X when premium pool is saturated.

[02:45] Priya: is that automatic or manual?

[02:49] Marco: can be automatic via routing policies — we have a policy engine. you can define fallback order: model-high -> model-quant8 -> model-low. and you can set region affinity.

[03:05] Lena: quick note — some transcripts from other calls showed this as "model fallback" or "fail open" but we call it graceful fallback to avoid confusion.

[03:18] [screenshare starts; Marco driving console] Marco: ok i'm in the console, top nav, we go to 'Keys & Quotas'. here you see org key at the top, then a table of project keys below. i'm going to click into 'project:recommendations' so you can see policy tiers.

[03:40] [03:40] Marco: sidebar note, we uploaded your sample traffic spreadsheet earlier — [link: /shared/celestia/traffic-sample.csv] — i've pre-loaded a suggested quota profile.

[03:52] Priya: i see the sample, nice. what's that 'adaptive burst' toggle?

[03:58] Marco: adaptive burst uses historical token smoothing — if a project has consistent bursts we allow higher short-term bursts, but if it's anomalous we clamp faster. it's driven by a moving window, default 24h.

[04:18] Ethan: does that rely on cookies or headers? how do we tie requests to a tenant?

[04:24] Marco: you key on API key and optional header x-org-id for finer sharding. requests are attributed at the gateway using the project key; you can map multiple service keys to one project.

[04:40] Samira: hostnames? we have multiple edge LB's — will rate enforcement be global?

[04:46] Marco: yes enforcement is global across our control plane and effector points — unless you deploy Private, then enforcement is in your VPC, same API semantics.

[05:00] Priya: show us the policy editor for auto-remediation/alerts.

[05:05] Marco: sure. click 'Alerts' then 'Guardrails'. here you can add thresholds and actions — e.g., when projectX uses >80% of daily quota, send slack, reduce burst to X, and flip routing to fallback model. i'll add a sample rule.

[05:28] Marco: done. action also supports webhooks to your incident platform.

[05:35] Priya: good — do you have RBAC so only platform team can edit these?

[05:40] Marco: yes, roles: org-admin, quota-manager, read-only. integrates with SAML/SSO.

[05:48] Samira: KMS — where are keys stored? we need HSM-backed key storage.

[05:54] Lena: we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault) and for Private we can support HSM. we'll attach a diagram in the follow-up pack.

[06:06] Ethan: latency impact of fallback to quantized model?

[06:10] Marco: quantized variants are typically slightly faster per-token — we reduce float32 compute but some tokens take marginally longer for certain ops; net effect usually improves latency/cost for most workloads. we can show benchmarks in the PoC.

[06:30] [07:00] Marco: switching to Optimize tab — this is our recommendation engine. it scans usage, suggests batch sizes, quantization levels, and cache cutoff lengths (prefix cache). for your chat-heavy workload, it recommends prefix KV cache = 64 tokens and batching 8 at peak.

[07:22] Priya: can Optimize simulate cost savings?

[07:26] Marco: yes — it runs a simulation based on your observed token distribution. the UI gives estimated monthly savings and a reliability delta.

[07:36] Priya: hmm that calcs looks optimistic, what's the confidence?

[07:40] Marco: we show confidence bands — low/med/high based on traffic variance. i'll attach the simulation export when we send the pilot template.

[07:52] Samira: security review: do you keep logs? are prompts persisted?

[07:58] Lena: by default Redwood retains request/response logs for operational debugging. for regulated customers we offer no-log modes and ability to route telemetry to customer S3 (private retention), plus audit logs delivered to your SIEM.

[08:18] Samira: is redaction supported?

[08:22] Marco: yes, we support server-side redaction hooks and client-side pre-send filtering. you can also set retention TTLs per project.

[08:36] Ethan: any built-in cost-control guardrails beyond quotas? like soft spend caps?

[08:42] Marco: we have soft spend caps that pause non-critical routes, and hard caps that block tokens. soft caps trigger notifications and autoscaling signals.

[08:56] [09:00] Marco: now demo of namespace routing: here i create a namespace 'eu-fin' and attach a project key; set region: eu-west, quota: 500k tokens/day, concurrency 40, burst 200 for 60s. then route rule prioritizes eu pool and falls back to us pool if eu is saturated.

[09:26] Priya: can we map multiple projects to one namespace?

[09:30] Marco: yes, namespace is just a logical grouping; projects can inherit namespace defaults and override. useful for team-level governance.

[09:44] Samira: what about audit logs for namespace-level changes? who changed quotas?

[09:50] Marco: all changes are recorded with user, IP, and optional change reason. audit trails are exportable.

[10:06] Priya: the screenshot you just showed — the console label said 'kay-v cache' spelled out, is that a transcription?

[10:12] Marco: (laughs) yeah, sometimes the auto transcriber writes "kay-v" — we mean KV cache (key-value).

[10:20] [10:30] Marco: a quick real-world scenario: team A has an ML feature that spikes at morning syncs; team B has a background job. we set projectA burst lane and projectB low concurrency. then org guardrail ensures org-level spend doesn't exceed budget by flipping non-critical routes to cheaper model. that preserves user-facing flows.

[10:54] Ethan: how fast is policy enforcement? near realtime?

[10:58] Marco: enforcement at the gateway is sub-second for concurrency limits, token counters are updated in the control-plane with <2s tail. burst enforcement uses local leaky buckets so reaction is immediate.

[11:18] Priya: curious on billing segmentation — can we bill per-project on our side?

[11:24] Lena: yes, billing exports include per-project token usage and cost allocation. for Dedicated we can provide per-pool metering.

[11:36] Samira: do you export PII redaction events? we need proof for audits.

[11:42] Marco: we keep a redaction log (metadata only) that indicates which request had redaction applied; payloads are not stored. we can include that in your audit export.

[11:56] [12:00] Marco: quick demo of 'what-if' simulator in the quotas section — i alter burst size from 200 to 100 and run a 24h replay using your sample traffic. shows expected drop in peak token spend and latency distribution.

[12:20] Priya: can we run that replay on a schedule?

[12:24] Marco: yes, replay jobs can be scheduled daily or on demand and results emailed.

[12:32] Ethan: any pre-built dashboard we can drop into Datadog?

[12:36] Marco: we push metrics via Datadog, Prometheus, or your SIEM. dashboards and example queries are in the docs pack.

[12:46] Samira: about SSO and admin onboarding — we have SCIM, do you support it?

[12:52] Lena: yep SCIM provisioning supported; roles map to our RBAC.

[13:00] [13:18] Priya: ok the PoC: we want to simulate noisy tenant attacks and measure cost, then test fallback routing and latency. can you run that in 2 weeks?

[13:28] Marco: yes — we'll provide a test harness. typical PoC includes bench scripts, a traffic replay, and a quick config sheet.

[13:36] Priya: K, you'll also need our sample of 2 weeks traffic, we'll share.

[13:40] Marco: perfect.

[13:48] [14:00] Marco: now short deep-dive on implementation patterns: pattern 1 — project-per-service: simple to bill, good isolation but potentially lots of keys. pattern 2 — namespace-per-region with subproject keys: good for compliance and routing. pattern 3 — hybrid: org key for infra, project keys for apps.

[14:26] Priya: we like pattern 2.

[14:30] Marco: great. we'll include sample terraform snippets for mapping that pattern.

[14:40] Samira: question: are you able to run in our VPC and still keep control plane in Redwood?

[14:46] Marco: yes — Private mode supports control plane redwood-managed with data plane in your VPC, or fully air-gapped on-prem if needed.

[14:58] Ethan: is there any functional difference in quota enforcement between hosted and Private?

[15:04] Marco: semantics are identical; the enforcement endpoints just live inside your network for Private.

[15:16] [15:20] Priya: can we tag tokens with business unit for chargeback?

[15:24] Marco: yes metadata tags on requests can be used for cost allocation.

[15:30] Samira: concerning data residence — if a request comes from EU user, can it be guaranteed to stay in EU?

[15:36] Marco: with regional pool pinning yes; we route by region affinity and show per-request region on request logs. for strict residency you should use Dedicated or Private with regionally pinned pools.

[15:50] Priya: demo question — i noticed an 'auto-throttle' toggle, what is the default behavior?

[15:56] Marco: default is off; when enabled it will auto-lower burst for anomalous projects and notify admins.

[16:10] [16:30] Marco: small hiccup — the UI lagged during the replay but it's just rendering, enforcement is not impacted (note: small UI glitch recorded).

[16:44] Priya: can clients get per-request headers indicating fallback status? we need to correlate degraded responses.

[16:50] Marco: yes, we add X-Redwood-Model and X-Redwood-Fallback headers to responses.

[16:58] Ethan: perfect for observability.

[17:04] Samira: compliance: ssl certs management?

[17:08] Marco: we support custom certs for Private, and managed certs for hosted.

[17:20] [17:30] Marco: jumping to Optimize again — one feature is 'suggested quantization profile' per model; for your inference shapes it suggests 8-bit quant + small batch for chat-heavy calls to balance latency and cost.

[17:48] Priya: can we pin certain customers to not be quantized (e.g., high fidelity)?

[17:52] Marco: yes, pinning by project key and adding a rule to exclude from fallback is supported.

[18:02] Priya: any API for programmatic policy updates?

[18:06] Marco: yes full REST APIs and terraform provider. we'll give you the git repo with examples.

[18:18] Priya: okay, let's talk about business cases — if we want 3 months of historical usage for the PoC, is that enough?

[18:24] Marco: that's usually sufficient to model burst patterns. if you have specific anomaly days include them.

[18:36] [18:40] Priya: Samira — any last security queries?

[18:44] Samira: audit retention windows, can we set retention windows per project?

[18:48] Marco: yes. default 90 days but adjustable down to 0 (no retention) or up to your enterprise tier retention.

[18:58] Ethan: will the PoC include a step that spawns 100 concurrent attackers to validate backpressure?

[19:04] Marco: yes that's part of our stress script.

[19:12] Priya: great.

[19:18] [19:30] Lena: quick recap so we have alignment: 1) we'll send pilot template + pricing, 2) we'll include SOC2 and architecture diagram, 3) we'll schedule the PoC run in two weeks. did i miss anything?

[19:48] Priya: add terraform snippets and replay harness.

[19:52] Marco: will do.

[20:00] Priya: also need a runbook for incident response when an org guardrail trips.

[20:06] Lena: good call — we'll include an incident playbook sample.

[20:12] Samira: can you also indicate expected SLA for Dedicated vs Hosted?

[20:18] Lena: yes, SLA doc will be in the pack.

[20:24] [20:30] Marco: small aside — competitor note: some folks we see try to implement similar things with API gateways + custom scripts, but they lack model-aware fallbacks and per-token metering.

[20:44] Priya: that was one of our concerns.

[20:50] Ethan: any limit on the number of project keys?

[20:54] Marco: none practical — thousands is fine, we recommend using namespace hierarchies to keep it organized.

[21:04] Priya: one more on billing: can you output usage daily?

[21:08] Lena: yes daily CSV with per-project granularity.

[21:16] [21:30] Marco: showing the export screens now.

[21:40] Priya: ok looks good. we'll want to keep an audit trail of changes during the PoC.

[21:46] Marco: audit is on by default for PoCs.

[21:52] [22:00] Samira: wondering about change approvals — does console support change approvals for quota updates?

[22:06] Marco: we have an approvals workflow; quotas above a threshold require two approvals. it integrates with your JIRA or ServiceNow via webhook.

[22:18] Priya: that's useful.

[22:26] Marco: small note, sometimes the automatic transcript labels one of our engineers as "Speaker 1" — ignore that in the UI notes.

[22:36] [23:00] Lena: open Q & A — anything else blocking on your side?

[23:06] Priya: budget approval is the main gating item internally; we'll know by end of next week if we can sign pilot.

[23:12] Lena: good. Marco and I will follow up with the pack.

[23:20] Ethan: related, do you have references for similar retail/fin use?

[23:26] Lena: yes we'll include two customer references; one in fintech and one in retail.

[23:34] Samira: do you have a whitepaper on quota playbooks?

[23:38] Marco: yes — "Quota Safeguard Playbook" — i'll attach.

[23:46] [24:00] Priya: ok let's wrap. thanks everyone.

[24:06] Lena: thanks all. recap in chat and we'll DM follow-ups.

[24:12] [END] Notes: transcript imperfect—occasional mis-attribution and filler words removed for legibility. shared artifacts: /shared/celestia/traffic-sample.csv, /shared/celestia/quota-playbook.pdf.
